Contract (k): %2E is an unreserved escape of '.', so the path to match normalizes to exactly /robots.txt; a URL whose normalized path is /robots.txt is allowed. The raw path /robots%2Etxt is not /robots.txt, so a raw-path comparison would fall through to these three Disallow rules (none of which matches it) instead of the implicit allow.

Contract (i): the space (U+0020) is ASCII outside the RFC 3986 character set, so the check is a check fault (check_invalid) and no access result is evaluated. Were it admitted, the path would be outside the three disallowed subtrees; the space cannot make any of them a prefix.
Contract (e): %61 is an unreserved escape of 'a' and is decoded before matching, so the path to match is /rfc/authors/team, which begins with the disallowed /rfc/authors/ subtree.

Contract (k): %72 is an unreserved escape of 'r' and decodes, so the path to match is exactly /robots.txt and the URL is allowed. The file's only rule covers /youtube/partner/, so no rule matches either the raw path or the normalized one; (k) makes the allow independent of that.

Contract (i): the double quote is ASCII outside the RFC 3986 character set, so the check is a check fault (check_invalid); no allow or disallow is evaluated. The path is outside the only disallowed subtree either way.
Contract (e): %70 is an unreserved escape of 'p', decoded before matching, so the path is /youtube/partner/docs and begins with the disallowed partner subtree.

Contract (k): %2E decodes to '.', so the path to match is exactly /robots.txt and the URL is allowed. Contract (e): %2E decodes to '.', so the path is /index.html; the group's Allow: / is a prefix rule covering every path on the host.
